text: The latest update did not improve battery life at all.
rationale: Tests whether the model picks up the negation cue or just the trigger word 'improve'

text: This app is no longer reliable on my phone.
rationale: Strong positive cue 'reliable' negated by 'no longer'; tests cue-vs-context handling

text: The team won the championship final last weekend.
rationale: Sports content unrelated to app-review training; tests domain-shift robustness

text: The service was not bad at all.
rationale: Double negation ('not bad') should result in a positive sentiment.

text: I can't say I disliked the interface.
rationale: Complex negation ('can't say I disliked') should be positive.

text: It failed to meet even the lowest expectations.
rationale: Negation via 'failed to' with a positive-ish word 'meet'.

text: The app didn't stop crashing until I reinstalled it.
rationale: Negation of 'stop crashing' tests if it sees the ongoing failure.

text: I wouldn't call this app user-friendly.
rationale: Explicit negation of a strong positive trait.

text: This is a masterpiece of bugs and crashes.
rationale: Uses 'masterpiece' (positive) in a negative context.

text: The support team is remarkably slow.
rationale: 'Remarkably' (often positive) used to intensify a negative trait.

text: I have a great deal of trouble with the login.
rationale: 'Great' (positive) used as a quantifier for 'trouble'.

text: It's a wonderful way to waste your time.
rationale: 'Wonderful' (positive) used sarcastically to describe a negative outcome.

text: The design is beautiful but the functionality is non-existent.
rationale: Positive trigger 'beautiful' contrasted with fatal flaw.

text: Add two eggs and whisk until fluffy.
rationale: Recipe domain; tests if neutral content is misclassified.

text: The stock market saw a sharp decline today.
rationale: Finance domain; checks for bias towards negative labels in news-like text.

text: The defendant pleaded not guilty to all charges.
rationale: Legal domain; checks if 'not guilty' (positive-ish) or 'charges' (negative-ish) dominates.

text: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
rationale: Scientific fact; should be strictly neutral.

text: He scored a goal in the final minute of the match.
rationale: Sports domain; checks for domain robustness.

text: Terrible.
rationale: Extremely short negative review.

text: Good.
rationale: Extremely short positive review.

text: Meh.
rationale: Extremely short neutral review.

text: A very long sentence repeating the same positive sentiment over and over again to see if the model gets lost in the noise of a hundred words that all mean the same thing but are just phrased slightly differently.
rationale: Tests if length dilutes the sentiment signal.

text: This app is quite literally the most frustrating piece of software I have ever had the misfortune of installing on any device I have ever owned in my entire life which spans several decades of using computers and mobile phones of all kinds.
rationale: Tests if long-winded frustration is captured.

text: Oh great another update that breaks everything.
rationale: Sarcastic use of 'great' to express frustration.

text: I love how the app deletes my data without asking.
rationale: Sarcastic use of 'love' for a data loss event.

text: Thanks for the useless notification at 3 AM.
rationale: Sarcastic 'thanks' for a negative experience.

text: Exactly what I needed a high-priced subscription for basic features.
rationale: Sarcastic 'exactly what I needed'.

text: Brilliant work making the UI even more confusing than before.
rationale: Sarcastic 'brilliant work'.

text: This app is totaly useles.
rationale: Misspelled words ('totaly', 'useles') test spelling robustness.

text: The best worst app ever.
rationale: Oxymoron/Irony testing.

text: I'm so hapy it finally works after 50 tries.
rationale: Positive sentiment with misspelling and context of prior failure.

text: 5/5 stars for the bugs.
rationale: Numerical rating logic used sarcastically in text.

text: The app is okay but could be better.
rationale: Mixed sentiment leaning towards neutral.
